issues.title: Create a dated backup branch of the current main
issues.body:
## Scope

If a branch already exists on origin that points to the current `main` tip, skip creating it and record that existing branch as the restore point instead.
Add a short entry to the existing rollback/versioning doc listing this branch as a restore point, described as the state after the texture/hair/tongue removal and the pose fixes. Restoring from it follows the existing method in that doc: make a branch from the backup and open a pull request into `main`.

UUID: f3e4d636-24e2-4974-b16b-2ac10dbf0572

issues.title: Generate the soft-tissue simulation proxy from the face mesh
issues.body:
## Scope

Add a build-time script that reads the neutral face mesh (default FaceCap) and produces a compact binary simulation asset committed to the static assets directory.
The script:
- simplifies the face surface to a coarse proxy, targeting a low thousands-range tetrahedron count with the target count configurable;
- creates an inner surface by offsetting the proxy inward along its normals by a configurable tissue thickness;
- splits each layer cell between the outer and inner surfaces into tetrahedra.
It labels inner-surface nodes as skull-attached or jaw-attached. Jaw-attached means below a configurable mouth-line boundary on the lower face. Outer nodes are labelled as skin.
It computes the render embedding: for every render-mesh vertex, the tetrahedron containing it, or the nearest one, and its barycentric weights.
The asset stores node positions, tetrahedra, edges, node labels, the embedding, and the render vertex count and a hash of the source mesh, so a mismatched face mesh is detected at load time. The script fails if it produces inverted or near-zero-volume tetrahedra or render vertices without an embedding.

## Files

New script under `scripts/`, new simulation asset in the static assets directory

issues.title: Implement the XPBD solver core
Run the solver in a Web Worker with a main-thread fallback
issues.body:
## Scope

Host the solver in a dedicated Web Worker running a fixed-timestep loop. Each frame the main thread sends pose targets and the jaw transform, and the worker returns node positions as transferable typed arrays. Do not rely on SharedArrayBuffer, because the static self-hosted deploy doesn't send the cross-origin isolation headers it needs.
Load the simulation asset once and validate its source-mesh hash and render vertex count against the loaded face mesh, reporting a mismatch as a diagnostic. If workers are unavailable, fall back to running the solver on the main thread at a reduced substep count. The worker must shut down cleanly when physics is turned off or the viewport unmounts.

## Files

New worker module and host bridge under `src/domain/physics/`, `vite.config.ts` if worker bundling needs it

## Dependencies

Depends on: XPBD solver core, simulation proxy asset

issues.title: Add the physics deformation provider and render embedding
issues.body:
## Scope

Register a new provider with id `xpbd-soft-tissue` in the provider registry, implementing the existing provider contract and producing vertex displacements.
Rendering uses the blendshape pose as today, plus a simulated offset: each node's simulated position minus its pose target, carried to render vertices through the embedding. This keeps the pose exact at rest and avoids applying the deformation twice.
`kinematic-blendshape` stays the default provider. Physics can be selected through the existing `VITE_DEFORMATION_PROVIDER` variable and switched on and off at runtime without reloading the mesh. Turning it off returns to pure kinematic output immediately. Controls, readout and the curve panel keep working the same either way. Add `VITE_SIM_PROXY_URL` for the simulation asset location, defaulting to the committed asset, and document it in the example env file.

## Files

`src/domain/providers/provider-registry.ts`, new provider under `src/domain/providers/`, `src/components/viewport/kinematic-provider-runtime.tsx`, `src/components/viewport/gltf-head-loader.ts`, `src/config/env.ts`, `.env.example`

issues.title: Establish physical units and the vertical axis for the face mesh
issues.body:
## Scope

Fix a single metres-per-source-unit scale for the face mesh. glTF assumes metres, so measure the loaded FaceCap face (width and height across the face) and check it against a plausible adult range. Record the scale explicitly. If the measurement is implausible, generation fails unless a scale is given explicitly.
Get the world vertical axis from the glTF scene's actual node transforms instead of assuming one. Store the scale, the axis and the existing normalization factor in the soft-tissue asset. Provide shared helpers that convert metres to proxy units and m/s² to proxy units per second squared, so every later conversion happens once, in one place.

## Files

Soft-tissue asset generation script under `scripts/`, `src/domain/physics/` unit-conversion helpers and asset loader

issues.title: Regenerate the proxy with 12 mm thickness, explicit inner–outer pairing and SI masses
issues.body:
## Scope

Regenerate the committed soft-tissue asset:
- **Thickness:** a tissue thickness of 0.012 m, converted to proxy units with the recorded scale. If the inward offset fails anywhere (expected risk areas are the nose and lips), do not thin the layer silently. Fail and report the source and proxy triangle indices, the centroid position, the normal, the requested thickness and the nearest facial region.
- **Pairing:** store an explicit table linking each outer node to its inner counterpart, instead of relying on how the nodes happen to be ordered.
- **Masses:** compute each node's mass from tetrahedron volumes in cubic metres. Each tetrahedron contributes volume × 1000 kg/m³ divided equally among its four corners. Store the resulting masses.
- **Format:** keep node labels for visualization only. Bump the asset format version, and make the loader reject older assets with a clear diagnostic.

## Files

Soft-tissue asset generation script under `scripts/`, `src/domain/physics/` asset loader, `public/data/facecap-soft-tissue.bin`, soft-tissue asset format doc under `docs/`

## Dependencies

Depends on: Physical units and vertical axis

UUID: 21986abe-0195-4b97-9236-f862bc8651d6

issues.title: Rework the solver so every node follows the pose, and remove the rigid jaw
issues.body:
## Scope

Change the solver model so the pose target is an exact equilibrium:
- **Dynamic nodes:** every node is dynamic, using the inverse of its stored mass.
- **Pose targets for all nodes:** every node gets a soft pose target. A skin node's target comes from the blendshape-posed surface as today. An inner node's target is its rest position plus its outer counterpart's displacement, so the whole layer moves with the expression.
- **Two stiffness settings:** inner nodes get a separate, much stiffer pose setting than skin nodes. Neither uses a hard pin.
- **Pose-relative edge lengths:** once per submitted frame, before the substeps, set every edge's rest length from the current pose-target positions. This covers all edges, not just skin-to-skin ones.
- **Remove the rigid jaw entirely:** the rotation, its pivot and 25° limit, the jaw settings, the jaw transform, and the hard jaw and skull attachments. Remove them from the solver frames, the worker messages, the host, the worker, the provider and the pose-target mapper. Jaw opening now comes only from the `jawOpen` blendshape, through the outer surface and the inner pairing.
- **SI gravity:** −9.81 m/s² along the recorded vertical axis, converted to proxy units once at initialization.
- **Retuned defaults:** retune the default stiffness and damping values for SI masses.
With gravity off, starting exactly at the pose target must produce no position correction and no velocity, for every pose and for slider mixes.

## Files

`src/domain/physics/` solver, pose-target mapper, worker messages, host and worker; `src/domain/providers/xpbd-soft-tissue-provider.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on: Forehead seam fix

issues.title: Apply simulation offsets to the original face geometry without copying it
issues.body:
## Scope

Change the physics render path so it no longer replaces the face geometry with a copy. While physics is on, add the simulation offset attribute directly to the original geometry, and copy only the material/shader that applies the offset. The offset must still be applied after the morph-target displacement.
When physics is turned off, reset or disposed, remove the attribute and restore the original material and culling state. The base and morph attributes are never recreated or replaced, so FaceCap's compressed, shared morph data stays exactly as loaded. With all offsets forced to zero, the render must be identical to the kinematic render.

## Files

`src/components/viewport/render-offset-layer.ts`, `src/components/viewport/render-offset-layer.test.ts`, `src/components/viewport/kinematic-provider-runtime.tsx`

issues.title: Bound render offsets for vertices outside the simulated tissue
issues.body:
## Scope

In the generated embedding:
- flag render vertices that lie outside every tetrahedron beyond a small tolerance. Give them the clamped nearest-point offset of the closest tetrahedron, faded out with distance, instead of extrapolated weights;
- exclude the teeth, inner mouth and eyes from simulation offsets, so they follow the blendshape pose only;
- give render vertices that share a position identical embeddings.
The generator fails if any embedded vertex can produce an offset larger than a configurable fraction of the local tissue thickness.

## Files

Soft-tissue asset generation script under `scripts/`, `src/domain/physics/` embedding, `public/data/facecap-soft-tissue.bin`

issues.title: Replace the physics tests to match the corrected model
issues.body:
## Scope

Remove or rewrite the existing tests that expect fixed skull and jaw attachments and a rigid jaw rotation. Add:
- **Exact equilibrium:** with gravity off and positions starting at the full targets, Neutral, Smile, AA and a slider mix produce no correction and no velocity.
- **Inner layer follows:** every inner node receives exactly its outer counterpart's pose displacement.
- **No rigid jaw:** changing `jawOpen` changes the targets only through the morph displacement, and no extra transform exists.
- **SI:** known tetrahedron volumes give the expected masses, and gravity converts correctly for the recorded scale.
- **Proxy diagnostics:** the 12 mm request either succeeds at the converted thickness or fails with a location-specific report.
- **Seam regression:** smooth forehead vertices are not split into disconnected parts, and offsets are continuous across the checked area.
- **Render-path and offset limits:** the zero-offset render matches the kinematic render, and the largest render offset stays under the configured limit.
- **Real browser, real FaceCap:** physics on, then cycle every expression plus Smile and AA. Check that there are no page or WebGL errors and no non-finite values, and compare canvas captures with gravity off against the kinematic capture within a tolerance. Turning physics off and on again must leave the mesh intact.
Update the benchmark script so it reports timing with all nodes dynamic.

## Files

`src/domain/physics/` unit tests, `src/components/viewport/render-offset-layer.test.ts`, `e2e/physics.spec.ts`, benchmark script under `scripts/`

## Dependencies

Depends on: All other issues in this task
